_notes: Ranges keyed by classification, not by individual offense. Offense nodes point here via their 'classification' + 'derived' flags.
nonViolentFelony tables apply when isVFO=false (routes to Article 70.00 / 70.06 / 70.10).

violentFelony tables apply when isVFO=true (routes to 70.02 / 70.04 / 70.08) -- now populated. SUNSET WARNING: PL 70.02(2)(a) and 70.04(2) determinate provisions are repealed September 1, 2027 and revert to indeterminate. Tables below reflect pre-sunset (current) law.
If an offense has a statute-specific sentencing carve-out (rare, e.g. certain weapon offenses), override at the offense level, not here.

persistentFelonyOffender_70_10.note: Discretionary. Court MAY sentence as Class A-I. Requires separate judicial finding, not automatic from 2 priors alone.

_notes: Determinate sentences; imposed in whole or half years per PL 70.02(2)(a) / 70.04(2), effective until September 1, 2027.
SUNSET: On September 1, 2027 these sections revert to indeterminate (NB Effective September 1, 2027 clauses). Regenerate this block after legislative update.
Post-release supervision (PRS) is mandatory on all determinate VFO sentences per PL 70.45: ClassB/C 2.5–5 years; ClassD/E 1.5–3 years. Source: PL 70.45 -- text not provided; flag for confirmation.

Class D VFO (70.02(2)(b)): sentence generally follows Class D felony provisions, but MUST be determinate when commitment to DOCCS is required (70.02(3)(c)). Range 2–7 years applies to DOCCS-commitment cases.

70.04 ClassD floor is 5 years (vs 70.02 ClassD floor of 2 years) per 70.04(3)(c). 70.04 ClassE floor is 3 years (vs 70.02 ClassE floor of 1.5 years) per 70.04(3)(d). Confirmed from provided 70.04 text.

70.08 ClassE: no provision in PL 70.08(3) for Class E violent felonies -- 70.08 only covers ClassA_II, ClassB, ClassC, ClassD. A persistent violent felony offender convicted of a ClassE VFO has no 70.08 minimum range. Flag for further legal research.

ClassD._note: Applies when DOCCS commitment required per 70.02(2)(b)/(3)(c); otherwise Class D felony provisions govern

_notes: Indeterminate sentence; maximum term is life imprisonment per PL 70.08(2). Minimum period fixed by court within statutory range per 70.08(3). Source: verbatim from provided PL 70.08 text.
SUNSET: Two versions of 70.08(3) exist. Pre-sunset (current, effective until September 1, 2027) has higher minimums. Post-sunset (effective September 1, 2027) has lower minimums. Both encoded below.
Class E violent felony: NO provision in PL 70.08(3). Statute only covers ClassA_II, ClassB, ClassC, ClassD. Persistent violent felony offender status for ClassE VFO -- gap; flag for legal research.

hateCrimeBump._note: Authoritative home for hate crime sentencing bump logic. Eligibility (isHateCrimeEligible) is determined by HATECRIME_LIST in ny_penal_ontology.json. This block defines what happens to the sentence once eligibility is confirmed and hate_crime_motivated is true.

misdemeanorOrClassCDE.effect: one category higher than base offense classification

ClassB.effect: fixed statutory minimum floors per predicate-offender status
ClassB._note: Not a simple one-class bump — court must apply 485.10(3) minimum floors based on prior record. Requires separate judicial finding.

ClassA_I.effect: flat minimum indeterminate period of at least 20 years
ClassA_I._note: Not a bump at all — applies a floor on the minimum period of an indeterminate sentence. See 485.10(4).
